item.text: The Independent Commission Against Corruption followed up NSW public sector agencies to assess progress in core prevention policies between 2001 and 2004.
item.support:
The main purpose of this research was to determine whether there had been progress 
by NSW public sector organisations

item.text: It examined codes of conduct, corruption risk management, internal audit, gifts and benefits policies, and internal investigations.
item.support:
The follow-up focussed 
on the areas of code of conduct, corruption risk management, internal audit, gifts and 
beneﬁ ts and internal investigations.

item.text: ICAC concluded that fewer agencies in the follow-up sample lacked the core strategies, but corruption risk management still needed further work.
item.support:
the main area in which further work 
needs to be done is corruption risk management.

item.text: ICAC cautioned that agencies’ answers were accepted at face value, the sample did not represent the whole sector and changes were not tested for statistical significance.
item.support:
All 
responses have been accepted at face value.

item.quote:
Finally, this follow-up research suggests that the main area in which further work 
needs to be done is corruption risk management.
